decision.summary: Tom gave one month's notice to leave 10 Nov. Under the Renters' Rights Act tenants must give two months, so it is not valid for 10 Nov; the earliest end is 10 Dec 2026. I replied to Tom and asked the landlord whether he will agree to 10 Nov in writing, with follow-up set for 14 Oct.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? What is the earliest end date?
answers.answer: Not as a one-month notice. Two months' written notice is required; served 10 Oct 2026, earliest end is 10 Dec 2026.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: Landlord agrees in writing to a shorter date (e.g. 10 Nov), i.e. a surrender by agreement. The tenant cannot unilaterally shorten it.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: Replied to Tom explaining the rule and that I am asking the landlord; asked Ben for written agreement by 14 Oct; follow-up scheduled. Deposit return via mydeposits after check-out, no date promised; keys arrangement to be confirmed.

conflicts: Tenant says one month's notice; current law requires two months.
assumptions: Notice treated as served 10 Oct 2026 by email; rent keeps running until the agreed end date.

args.body: Hi Tom, thanks for letting us know, and good luck with the new job. Since 1 May 2026 tenants need to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough on its own. Your notice, received 10 October, would end the tenancy on 10 December 2026 at the earliest. You can leave earlier only if your landlord agrees in writing. I'm asking him now whether he will agree to 10 November, and I'll tell you his answer by Wednesday 14 October. Please keep paying rent as normal until an end date is agreed in writing. On keys and your deposit: I'll confirm the key hand-back arrangements once the end date is settled. Your deposit is held in the mydeposits scheme and is returned after you leave, once the final check of the flat is done. I can't give a firm date or amount yet. Kind regards, Mare & Co Lettings
